primary_evidence: linux-ci-44148898104: one hosted runner, clean baseline/candidate builds, seeded interleaved variants, three independent 5-second cases per group
limits: All 18 tool-observed source checkouts were clean. Windows candidate builds at b5459bc contain product code 508d39c; the external plan separately asserts that product revision.
All binaries still print ling 0.1.7 because the product version had not yet been bumped. Compare the exact revision, source hashes and binary hash.
Windows supports Fast only; Reliable is not executed and never counted as a pass.
Each trial has its own nearest-rank percentiles recomputed from raw samples. Three-run median/min/max never pools repetition samples.

Idle scenarios are serial closed-loop PING with 0, 1 or 100 idle subscriptions. Backlog is confirmed EVENT/ACK throughput after 20,000 preloaded events, max pending 128; no per-ACK latency samples exist.
Five-second runs, three repeats, same-host loopback and Python client limits do not establish statistical significance, sustained capacity or deployment performance.
Linux server CPUs 0/1 and client CPUs 2/3 are disjoint logical affinity sets. Hardware reports two cores with SMT; logical affinity is not proof of physically separate cores.
Linux ext4 data=writeback,nobarrier,journal_async_commit measures software fsync calls, not physical power-loss durability.
Windows CPU counters have short-sample quantization and some zero deltas; zero is not evidence of zero cost. Windows has no CPU affinity isolation.
Backlog server CPU seconds rise with the much larger completed workload. CPU per success is also retained and does not isolate scheduling, syscall or journal cost.

analysis.linux_backlog_regression: Not reproduced after TCP_NODELAY: all three Fast on runs exceed 3,533 ACK/s and all Reliable on runs exceed 2,452 ACK/s, versus about 100/101 legacy. First-round evidence remains in the sibling v020-2026-11-18 archive.
analysis.linux_idle100_tradeoff: On reduces polling to zero, server CPU and PING P99/P99.9; median closed-loop PING throughput still falls about 11.45% Fast and 13.38% Reliable.
analysis.windows_tail_regression: Fast idle100 on median P99 +31.24% and P99.9 +12.41% versus legacy, with PING rate +8.23%. Idle0 on P99 +10.88% and P99.9 +1.31%; idle1 tails improve. Preserve all repeats and disclose the regression; Linux does not show the same pattern.
analysis.causality_limit: The clean candidate includes TCP_NODELAY and same-run legacy/off/on comparisons support the chosen mitigation. No packet trace or per-ACK timings were captured, so this is not proof of a particular delayed-ACK timer mechanism.
